name.text: How many points two loci share

questiontext.text:
For each pair of loci, decide how many points they share.

  1. [[if test="is(ty[1]=3)"]]A circle of radius \({@rw[1][2]@}\) cm and a straight line \({@rw[1][3]@}\) cm from its centre[[elif test="is(rw[1][4]=0)"]]Two circles of radii \({@rw[1][2]@}\) cm and \({@rw[1][3]@}\) cm with the same centre[[else]]Two circles of radii \({@rw[1][2]@}\) cm and \({@rw[1][3]@}\) cm whose centres are \({@rw[1][4]@}\) cm apart[[/if]]

    [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

  2. [[if test="is(ty[2]=3)"]]A circle of radius \({@rw[2][2]@}\) cm and a straight line \({@rw[2][3]@}\) cm from its centre[[elif test="is(rw[2][4]=0)"]]Two circles of radii \({@rw[2][2]@}\) cm and \({@rw[2][3]@}\) cm with the same centre[[else]]Two circles of radii \({@rw[2][2]@}\) cm and \({@rw[2][3]@}\) cm whose centres are \({@rw[2][4]@}\) cm apart[[/if]]

    [[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

  3. [[if test="is(ty[3]=3)"]]A circle of radius \({@rw[3][2]@}\) cm and a straight line \({@rw[3][3]@}\) cm from its centre[[elif test="is(rw[3][4]=0)"]]Two circles of radii \({@rw[3][2]@}\) cm and \({@rw[3][3]@}\) cm with the same centre[[else]]Two circles of radii \({@rw[3][2]@}\) cm and \({@rw[3][3]@}\) cm whose centres are \({@rw[3][4]@}\) cm apart[[/if]]

    [[input:ans3]] [[validation:ans3]] [[feedback:prt3]]

  4. [[if test="is(ty[4]=3)"]]A circle of radius \({@rw[4][2]@}\) cm and a straight line \({@rw[4][3]@}\) cm from its centre[[elif test="is(rw[4][4]=0)"]]Two circles of radii \({@rw[4][2]@}\) cm and \({@rw[4][3]@}\) cm with the same centre[[else]]Two circles of radii \({@rw[4][2]@}\) cm and \({@rw[4][3]@}\) cm whose centres are \({@rw[4][4]@}\) cm apart[[/if]]

    [[input:ans4]] [[validation:ans4]] [[feedback:prt4]]

generalfeedback.text:
Two circles of radii \(r_1\) and \(r_2\) with centres \(d\) apart meet at two points when \(|r_1 - r_2| \lt d \lt r_1 + r_2\), at one point when \(d = r_1 + r_2\) or \(d = |r_1 - r_2|\), and not at all otherwise. A circle of radius \(r\) and a line \(p\) from its centre meet twice when \(p \lt r\), once (a tangent) when \(p = r\), and not at all when \(p \gt r\).

  1. [[if test="is(ty[1]=3)"]]The distance from the centre to the line, \({@rw[1][3]@}\) cm, is [[if test="is(cats[1]=1)"]]more than the radius, \({@rw[1][2]@}\) cm: the line misses the circle.[[elif test="is(cats[1]=2)"]]equal to the radius: the line is a tangent and touches the circle at one point.[[else]]less than the radius, \({@rw[1][2]@}\) cm: the line cuts the circle twice.[[/if]][[elif test="is(ty[1]=1)"]][[if test="is(rw[1][4]=0)"]]The circles have the same centre and different radii, so the smaller circle is inside the larger one.[[else]]The centres are \({@rw[1][4]@}\) cm apart, less than \({@rw[1][2]@} + {@rw[1][3]@}\), but also less than the difference of the radii, \({@abs(rw[1][2]-rw[1][3])@}\) cm: the smaller circle is inside the larger one.[[/if]][[elif test="is(ty[1]=2)"]][[if test="is(rw[1][4]=rw[1][2]+rw[1][3])"]]\({@rw[1][4]@} = {@rw[1][2]@} + {@rw[1][3]@}\) exactly, so the circles just touch at one point.[[else]]\({@rw[1][4]@}\) is exactly the difference of the radii, \({@max(rw[1][2],rw[1][3])@} - {@min(rw[1][2],rw[1][3])@}\), so the circles just touch at one point.[[/if]][[else]][[if test="is(cats[1]=3)"]]The distance between the centres, \({@rw[1][4]@}\) cm, is between the difference of the radii, \({@abs(rw[1][2]-rw[1][3])@}\) cm, and their sum, \({@rw[1][2]+rw[1][3]@}\) cm, so the circles cross twice.[[else]]The distance between the centres, \({@rw[1][4]@}\) cm, is more than the sum of the radii, \({@rw[1][2]+rw[1][3]@}\) cm, so the circles are apart.[[/if]][[/if]]

  2.   3. questiondescription.text:
Loci: how many points two loci share

Grade 12 CBE Core 2.3: Decide how many points two circles, or a circle and a line, share by comparing distances.

Core

This question is original to this project.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Core Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).

truefeedback.text: [[if test="is(ty[1]=3)"]][[if test="is(ans1=\"none\")"]]No points would mean the line is further from the centre than the radius. Here the line is \({@rw[1][3]@}\) cm from the centre and the radius is \({@rw[1][2]@}\) cm.[[elif test="is(ans1=\"one\")"]]Exactly one point would mean the line is a tangent, exactly one radius from the centre. Here the line is \({@rw[1][3]@}\) cm from the centre and the radius is \({@rw[1][2]@}\) cm.[[else]]Two points would mean the line passes closer to the centre than the radius. Here the line is \({@rw[1][3]@}\) cm from the centre and the radius is \({@rw[1][2]@}\) cm.[[/if]][[else]][[if test="is(ans1=\"none\")"]]No points would mean the circles are apart (centres further apart than the sum of the radii) or one is inside the other (centres closer than the difference of the radii).
